title: KwizMe
tagline: A study tool that turns your lecture PDFs into practice quizzes you can retake.
result: No account needed: an anonymous visitor uploads a deck, gets five quizzes a day, and retakes them in the browser.
problem: Students revising from their own lecture notes have no practice questions, so they re-read material instead of testing themselves, which retains less. Writing questions by hand from a long deck is slow enough that most people skip it, and the generic question banks that do exist are not about the material they were actually taught. architecture: `/api/generate-quiz` accepts an uploaded PDF, image or text file, checks type and page count with pdf-lib, and sends the extracted content to Gemini 2.5 Flash with a JSON response type so the reply is parseable by contract rather than by regex. A deterministic `validateQuizResponse` pass rejects a malformed or short-count response before anything is stored. A second, cooler model call at temperature 0.3 does nothing but tidy the quiz description, which keeps the expensive call at 0.7 focused on questions and gives it a 60k output ceiling, because truncation was the failure that mattered.

The boundary that shapes the codebase is anonymous versus signed in. `storage-router.ts` and `session-storage-router.ts` present one API for save, read and delete, then route to browser storage for anonymous users or to Supabase Postgres for authenticated ones, where eight tables carry row-level security. Rate limiting mirrors the same split: five generations a day, keyed by IP when there is no account and by user id when there is, with per-user overrides in a `user_limits` table.

diagram.caption: One router decides where a quiz lives; nothing else knows.

decisions.because: someone can finish the whole loop before creating an account, at the cost of a second storage path that has to stay in step with Postgres.

decisions.chose: A JSON response type from the model
decisions.because: the reply is parseable by contract, and a deterministic validator can reject the rest before it reaches a table.

decisions.over: filtering by user id in application code
decisions.because: a query someone forgets to filter cannot leak another student's quizzes, accepting policies that have to be tested in SQL.
every generation costs a model call, accepting that people behind one network share a quota.

impact: Because nothing is gated, the funnel starts at first use rather than at signup, and a visitor who never registers still gets the full loop. It carries what a launched app needs rather than what a demo needs: Sentry error capture, Discord alerts on signup, generation and failure, health endpoints for both the app and the database, and a public status page.
